I'm also constantly exhausted; even a simple shower feels like running a marathon, so I end up just sitting in my chair for hours because I have no energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about your thoughts and feelings about your mother's passing, and do you often find yourself thinking about her or wishing you could have done something differently?\n\nPatient: Her unexpected passing ten months ago has left me with an overwhelming guilt, and I've become convinced her death was actually a punishment from God directed at me. I even hear her voice scolding me in the hallway, saying I ruined everything and am just a burden now. It makes me feel like everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about these voices you hear, like your mother's, and how often you hear them, to help me understand what you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: I hear my mother's voice clear as day scolding me in the hallway, mostly at night when the house gets really quiet. She says things like, \"You ruined everything, Barbara,\" or \"You’re a burden to everyone now.\" I know she is gone and that no one else hears it, but it still sounds so real to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you also see things that aren't there, like shadows or your mother's image, or is it just her voice that you hear?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see any shadows or my mother's image at all. It is strictly just her voice that I hear scolding me in the hallway when the house gets quiet. I've never seen anything that isn't there, it's only the sound of her voice.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear, your mother's voice, is a real voice that others should be able to hear as well, or do you understand it as a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: I know she is gone and that no one else in the house can hear her, so I understand that others shouldn't be able to hear it. But when it happens, it sounds so clear and real to me that it's hard to explain. It just feels like it's happening right there in the hallway.\n\nDoctor: When you hear your mother's voice, do you think it's coming from inside your mind or from outside, like it's actually happening in the hallway?\n\nPatient: It feels like it is coming from outside my head, clear as day right there in the hallway. Even though I logically know my mother is gone and others can't hear it, it sounds like she is actually standing there scolding me. She tells me so clearly that I ruined everything and that I'm just a burden to everyone now.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think that these voices or the guilt you feel might be a part of your own thoughts or feelings, rather than an actual reflection of reality or your mother's true opinions?\n\nPatient: Logically, I know she's gone and people tell me these things are just in my head, but in those quiet moments, the guilt feels absolutely true. Her voice sounds so incredibly real that I can't help but believe what she's saying about me. It just feels like I really did ruin everything, even if I try to tell myself otherwise.\n\nDoctor: When you hear your mother's voice, even though you know it's not real to others, do you think it's possible that your mind is playing a trick on you, or do you still believe it's actually your mother trying to communicate with you?\n\nPatient: Intellectually, I know my mother is gone and no one else can hear her, so it must be my mind playing tricks on me. But in the quiet of the night, the voice sounds so incredibly real and hurtful. It just makes me feel like such a burden to everyone.\n\nDoctor: When you're hearing your mother's voice and feeling this overwhelming guilt, do you ever feel like you're losing touch with what's real and what's not, or do you always have a sense that these experiences, although very real-feeling, are not actually happening in the external world?\n\nPatient: While I logically know my mother is gone and others can't hear her voice, it still feels incredibly real to me. But beyond that, I am deeply convinced that the signs from God, like the church bells ringing off-time and the flickering streetlight outside, are real messages meant just for me. Even though people try to tell me it's all in my head, I truly believe those signs are real."
